lines: Unintentional weight loss and intermittent abdominal discomfort over 3 months

This 69-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and chronic lower back pain presents to Gastroenterology three months following his January 2020 Cardiology evaluation.
He presents for evaluation following unintentional weight loss and intermittent abdominal discomfort over the past 3 months.
He reports changes in bowel habits, including occasional loose stools and a sensation of incomplete evacuation.
He denies overt rectal bleeding but describes dark stools on a few occasions.
Past medical history includes type 2 diabetes and hypertension, both well controlled.
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily at bedtime
- Warfarin 5 mg PO daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Morphine Sulfate SR 30 mg PO twice daily
- Paternal uncle: Colon cancer diagnosed age 75

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech

lines: Sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech

This 71-year-old male with hypertension, diabetes, and history of atrial fibrillation (previously evaluated in Cardiology and multiple ED visits) presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech that began two hours ago while watching television.
His wife reports that he was in his usual state of health earlier in the day.
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily at bedtime
- Warfarin 5 mg PO daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Morphine Sulfate SR 30 mg PO twice daily
- Paternal uncle: Colon cancer diagnosed age 75
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago after 30 pack-year history.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month.
On examination, the patient's blood pressure is 165/95 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and he is afebrile.
Neurological examination reveals left facial droop, left arm and leg weakness, and dysarthria.
His NIH Stroke Scale score is 12.
A noncontrast CT scan of the head is performed immediately and shows no hemorrhage or other acute abnormalities.
